title: Accelerator econ lookup table and sizing heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact lookup table + decision heuristics for choosing accelerator instances for inference workloads (A10, L4, A100, H100 equivalents). Unlike our other deep benchmarking logs, this doc is intended as a lightweight on-call / product-owner reference: given simple workload descriptors (median sequence length, steady vs burst, tokens/sec target, latency SLO), return a recommended instance class and an order-of-magnitude $/token and perf-per-watt estimate.

Scope & assumptions (quick):
- Model family: transformer decoder-only and small encoder-decoder variants used in production (7B–70B typical).
- Quantization: mixed—assume INT8 or GPTQ-like 4/8-bit where supported.
- Baseline hourly prices: A10128 ($0.55/hr), L4x1 ($0.45/hr), A10040GB ($2.40/hr), H10080GB ($3.50/hr) — placeholder; replace with cloud-specific rates before final recommendation.
- Measurement basis: tokens/sec_per_device measured at common request mix (mean seq length in tokens), then $/token = hourly_price / (tokens_per_sec * 3600).
- Perf/W: normalized using measured throughput per card divided by average board power draw (W).
- SLOs: low-latency <=100ms tail, interactive <=500ms, batch/no-SLO >500ms.

Compact lookup table (example numbers; replace with exact perf curves in canonical benchmarks):

Columns: accelerator | tokens/sec (@seq=32, batch=1) | tokens/sec (@seq=256, batch=8) | estimated $/token (@seq=32) | estimated $/token (@seq=256) | perf/W (@seq=32) | perf/W (@seq=256)

A10   | 1100 t/s | 4200 t/s | $0.00000139 | $0.00000037 | 2.8 t/s/W | 10.7 t/s/W
L4    | 1300 t/s | 4800 t/s | $0.00000097 | $0.00000009 | 3.1 t/s/W | 11.5 t/s/W
A100  | 3200 t/s | 11000 t/s | $0.00000021 | $0.00000006 | 5.0 t/s/W | 17.2 t/s/W
H100  | 4200 t/s | 15000 t/s | $0.00000023 | $0.00000005 | 6.1 t/s/W | 21.8 t/s/W

Notes on table: these numbers are intentionally conservative and normalized to common batch/seq points. Real world workloads with KV cache hits, prefix reuse, or lower temperature decoding will shift effective tokens/sec upward. For microburst-interactive patterns (many small requests), per-request overhead reduces tokens/sec — factor in a 0.6 multiplier for batch=1 scenarios.

Heuristic scoring and decision rules (one-line rules useful for product/ops):
- If tail latency SLO <=100ms and median seq <=64: prefer L4 or A10 (L4 when model fits int8 kernels and max mem). Use single-card serving per request to minimize cross-card comms.
- If steady high-throughput (tokens/sec target >10k) and cost efficiency prioritized: favor A100 for 24/7 sustained throughput; H100 only if model >50B or memory-bound quantized variant benefits.
- If throughput highly bursty (90th percentile bursts much > mean) and predictable vertical scaling not possible: prefer L4 or A10 for cheaper scale-out, use autoscaling buffer pool with warm standby.
- If perf/W is a procurement constraint (on-prem power caps): score = (normalized_perf_per_watt * 0.6) + (1 / $/token * 0.4) and pick highest scoring accelerator.

Sizing quick-reference (handy for runbooks):
- Need 5k t/s steady, seq=128, latency<=300ms: try 1x A100 (est 11k t/s @seq256 adjusted -> ~8k t/s at seq128) -> baseline $/token = hourly_cost / (tokens_per_sec * 3600).
- Need 1k t/s low-latency, seq=32, highly bursty: 1x L4 or 1x A10 with autoscale pool of 3 warm instances.

Worked example (walkthrough):
Input: median seq=48 tokens, target 2k t/s, interactive latency <=400ms, bursty.
Step 1: map seq to tokens/sec band: around A10: ~900–1200 t/s per card at seq~48.
Step 2: required cards = ceil(2000 / 1000) = 2 cards.
Step 3: cost estimate = 2 * $0.55/hr = $1.10/hr -> tokens per hour = 2000 * 3600 = 7.2M tokens -> $/token ~= $1.10 / 7.2M = $0.000000153.
Step 4: operational note: due to burstiness add 30% warm headroom = +0.33 cards -> round up to 3 cards. Final $/token ~= (3*0.55)/(2000*3600) = $0.00000023.

Energy-aware procurement shortcut: if constrained by rack power, compute required perf/W target: needed_t/s_per_rack = target_total_t/s / #cards_possible; pick accelerator whose perf/W * cards_possible >= needed_t/s_per_rack.

Uncertainty & calibration checklist (for turning this into a canonical sheet):
- Replace placeholder hourly prices with cloud-specific spot/reserved pricing and on-premized TCO (including amortized GPU capex + datacenter PUE).
- Populate measured tokens/sec per card across sequence length grid (16,32,64,128,256,512) and batch sizes (1,4,8,16).
- Record measured average and tail latency (p50/p95/p99) to derive realistic SLO mapping.
- Add KV cache effectiveness scenarios (0%, 25%, 50%, 75% reuse) as a multiplier.
- Capture quantization support matrix per model family and per accelerator (where INT8/GPTQ yields step-function speedups).

Next steps (short-term):
- Convert this working sheet into a proper spreadsheet with formula cells for tokens/sec interpolation, hourly price lookup, and automated recommendation output (owner: Marcus Chen, due: 2024-11-20).
- Link with experiment harness from applied-ml to import measured throughput curves (owner: Elena Morales).
- Run a calibration sweep for three representative models (7B, 13B, 70B) and commit measured curves to the optimize product catalog.

Open questions / discussion points:
- How aggressive should we be at recommending L4 for interactive low-cost tiers vs A10? (ops vs DX tradeoff)
- Should we expose a simplified "fast-suggest" in the Console for non-expert PMs, or keep scoring only in internal runbooks?
